official.deadline_note: National deadline by which French institutions must submit application files to Campus France (mercredi 6 janvier 2027 inclus); the calendar does not apply to students, who must ask their host French institution for its own internal deadline, which comes earlier
official.status_note: Campus France's institutional page states 'L'appel a candidatures 2027 est ouvert' (2027 call for applications is open); laureates and institutions will be notified of results by email during the week of 12 April 2027
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'For both elements of the program, tuition fees are not covered by the France Excellence Eiffel program.' The regulations add that tuition is not paid at either level, though recipients of a French government scholarship are exempt from tuition fees for a national degree or 'diplome d'ingenieur' at public institutions under the Ministry of Higher Education (Article R719-49 of the Education Code), and course fees are not covered
benefits: Monthly allowance at master's level: EUR 1,200 (from January 2026)

Doctorate level: monthly allowance published by Campus France as EUR 2,100 (from January 2026) on the English programme page and EUR 2,000 (effective 1 January 2026) in the 2027-session regulations and on the French programme page
Certain direct services: international transportation, national transportation, insurance, housing search, cultural activities
Support throughout the duration of the stay and access to the Eiffel Alumni community
eligibility: The programme is reserved for international students; candidates with dual nationality, one of which is French, are not eligible
Master's level: candidates must be 29 years old or younger; doctoral level: 35 years old or younger
Candidates currently studying in France are ineligible at graduate level; at postgraduate level, students currently studying abroad are a priority over those already residing in France

Only programmes delivered in France that award a nationally accredited master's degree, engineering diploma, or doctoral degree (cotutelle/co-direction with a partner institution abroad); French programmes located abroad are not accepted
Cannot be combined with another French government scholarship, an Erasmus+ scholarship, or a scholarship from the Agence Universitaire de la Francophonie
requirements: Each recipient must be officially enrolled at the French institution that submitted the application
Applications must be presented by a French higher education institution; applications sent directly by students or transmitted by foreign institutions are declared ineligible
36-month doctoral awards are reserved for new candidates enrolling in the first year of a doctoral programme who are not already studying in France
Recipients must meet the academic requirements of each successive year of the programme to continue receiving benefits; a repeated year due to failure suspends the scholarship
documents: Candidate commitment form (engagement du candidat), signed by the candidate and transmitted by the institution
Signed 'bordereau' listing all applications submitted by the institution, in PDF format

After selection: certificate of academic enrollment and certification of enrollment in the national health insurance scheme (Securite Sociale or CEAM) submitted to Campus France within two months of arrival
Two academic-progress documents per year signed by the institution: an end-of-first-semester evaluation form and an end-of-year performance form (or doctoral committee report)
selection_criteria: The candidate's track record of excellence
The institution's reputation abroad and its international student policy
The institution's policy of cooperation and partnership with the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Review by expert panels of teacher-researchers (holders of the HDR for the doctoral component), one panel per field of study, based on published evaluation grids
coverage: Monthly living allowance: EUR 1,200 at master's level (doctoral level as published by Campus France, see benefits)

International travel: airfare in the least expensive class between the international airport closest to the recipient's home country and the academic location in France, reimbursed upon presentation of receipts up to 50% of the maximum rate set by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, plus second-class train or bus travel from the arrival airport to the academic location
Return travel at the end of the programme in the least expensive class, requestable within 12 months of the scholarship's end and conditional on receipt of the final-year academic results
Health insurance: enrollment in a temporary health insurance plan until French national scheme coverage takes effect, then a supplemental scheme at no cost to the recipient
Housing search assistance (choice of CROUS student dormitories or private homes) and cultural activities/outings
Tuition fees and course fees are not covered
application_method: Contact Campus France in the country of origin or the French Embassy's cooperation and cultural action service for guidance on study plans
Contact the international relations department of a French institution (website, email or telephone) to learn the procedures and deadline; the student chooses the institution
The institution accepts and supports the application and submits it online via the dedicated Campus France website
Only French higher education institutions can submit applications; all French institutions are eligible to submit
official.application_route: Indirect nomination: a French higher education institution must select the candidate and submit the file to Campus France during the open call (2027 session: opened 2 October 2026, institutional deadline 6 January 2027); direct applications by students or foreign institutions are ineligible
official.study_mode: Full-time enrolment in a nationally accredited master's, engineering or doctoral programme; signing an apprenticeship or professional training contract terminates the scholarship
official.citizenship_residency: Reserved for non-French international students; dual French nationality excluded; master's candidates currently studying in France are ineligible and 36-month doctoral awards require candidates not already studying in France
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is reserved for foreign students; French nationality (or dual French nationality) is a bar
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Seven priority fields only - Science and Technology: Biology and Health, Ecological Transition, Mathematics and Digital Technology, Engineering Sciences; Humanities and Social Sciences: French History/Language/Civilization, Law and Political Science, Economics and Management
official.research_requirement: Doctoral component requires enrolment in a joint-supervision (cotutelle) or dual-degree doctoral programme with a partner institution abroad; 36-month awards are limited to new first-year doctoral candidates not already studying in France
official.duration: Master's: maximum 12 months (M2 entry), 24 months (M1 entry) or 36 months (engineering degree); Doctoral: 12, 18 or 36 months from 1 September of the award year; the study period must begin between 1 September and 30 November and the start date cannot be postponed
official.description: A programme of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, managed by Campus France, that enables French higher education institutions to attract the best foreign students to their master's and doctoral programmes, training future foreign decision-makers from the public and private sectors in priority fields of study. Applications are presented exclusively by French higher education institutions and are competitive, with recipients selected for excellence.
official.program_type: Master's degree, engineering diploma, and doctoral degree (joint supervision / dual degree)

not_confirmed: english_requirement - no central English-language requirement is published; language requirements are set by each programme and host institution

doctoral monthly allowance - Campus France's English programme page states EUR 2,100 (from January 2026) while the 2027-session regulations PDF and the French programme page state EUR 2,000 (effective 1 January 2026); the master's figure of EUR 1,200 is confirmed by all official sources

exact checklist of documents for the institution's nomination file - only the commitment form and signed 'bordereau' are named on the official pages; remaining file contents are set by each institution
internal deadlines of individual French institutions - not published centrally; institutions set their own earlier cut-off for student candidacies
verification.notes: Checked the Campus France (awarding body) student pages in English and French, the institutional page carrying the 2027-session calendar, and the official Eiffel 2027 regulations PDF; the English institutions page still shows the closed 2026 campaign (deadline 8 January 2026) while the French institutions page (updated 2 October 2026) publishes the live 2027 calendar used here.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply for the Eiffel Excellence Scholarship directly - a French higher education institution must nominate and submit your file to Campus France, so the decisive step is winning an institution's sponsorship months before the 6 January 2027 deadline. Expect a monthly living allowance of EUR 1,200 (master's) or roughly EUR 2,000-2,100 (doctorate) plus covered international and domestic travel, health insurance and housing support, but you must fund your own tuition. The 2027 session opened on 2 October 2026 and results only arrive the week of 12 April 2027, so keep alternative funding warm until then.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving master's or PhD applicants aged 29/35 or under, studying outside France, in one of the seven priority fields, who can persuade a French institution to champion their nomination.
application_readiness_checklist: Email the international relations offices of target French institutions first, asking explicitly whether they will submit an Eiffel nomination for you and what their internal deadline is
Confirm your programme sits in one of the seven eligible fields, awards a nationally accredited degree, and is delivered in France
Check the age limits (29 at master's, 35 at doctoral) and that you hold no other French government, Erasmus+ or AUF funding
Build an excellence-led file - transcripts, CV and a study/research project tied to the institution's own priorities - well before the institution's internal cut-off
Line up a backup funding plan now, since Eiffel results are only published in mid-April for a September start
common_rejection_risks: Submitting an application yourself or through a foreign institution - these are declared ineligible
Waiting for the 6 January 2027 national deadline instead of the host institution's earlier internal cut-off
Holding another French government, Erasmus+ or Agence Universitaire de la Francophonie scholarship
Being currently enrolled in France at master's level, or exceeding the 29/35 age limits
Signing an apprenticeship or professional training contract, which automatically terminates the scholarship
Changing degree subject or institution after the award - only same-field changes at the same institution preserve payments
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and course fees (not covered, though holders are exempt from tuition for national degrees at public institutions), the CVEC student contribution, any pre-sessional language training (the months of allowance cover at most one month of language training and its cost is yours), and everyday living costs in expensive cities such as Paris where the stipend may fall short.
document_audit: Two institution-side items you must chase: your signed 'engagement du candidat' (candidate commitment form) and the institution's signed 'bordereau' listing your application
Proof of enrollment in the French national health insurance scheme must reach Campus France within two months of arrival or payments can be suspended - register at etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr promptly
Keep every flight and train ticket: travel is reimbursed only against receipts, capped at 50% of the ministry's maximum rate for your country
First stipend arrives only after you physically begin studies in France and a French bank account is in place (first payment sent via Western Union)
alerts: 2027-session timeline: call opened 2 October 2026, institutions must submit by 6 January 2027 inclusive, results the week of 12 April 2027 - late results can collide with visa and housing timelines
The funded study period must start between 1 September and 30 November of the award year and cannot be postponed
36-month doctoral funding is reserved for new first-year doctoral students not already studying in France
An internship abroad suspends payments for the time spent outside France, and an internship taken in your home country ends the scholarship
Only one gap year of up to one year is permitted, requested at least two months in advance, and it suspends both allowance and scholarship-holder status
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Student secures institutional support, the French institution files the nomination online through Campus France during the open call, expert panels per field review the file, and Campus France informs laureates and institutions by email the week of 12 April 2027.
